mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 2000K units signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative 20-day forward returns observed during such periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average by more than 5% for four consecutive months indicates supply-side contraction, which raises input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during these episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth above 1% month-over-month, combined with a simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5%, signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressure and cost of capital, resulting in positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward returns in such episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the real savings rate (RSAFS) above its 5-year average by more than 2 percentage points indicates households are saving more relative to income, reducing consumption and investment demand, which drives negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 5Y avg(RSAFS) + 2pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during these periods (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% simultaneously for two months signals a disinflationary easing, which lowers real interest rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls AND CPIAUCSL < 2% for two months
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward returns during such coordinated disinflationary episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 4% for three consecutive months signals a robust supply expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of such sustained industrial production expansion (p > 0.05).
